choices.reason: m72 at 5/1 provides an intermediate solvent-strength anchor for a scaffold with large observed condition-dependent tails, helping learn the onset of its nonlinear response.
m3 is a donor-free aromatic control at 5/1 and high loading, useful for testing whether strong-ratio corrections transfer to weakly interacting polyaromatics.
m55 at 10/1 extends the measured m55 condition curve between ordinary and stronger PE regimes, complementing observed m55 rows such as 7937e75a777f4bf48438.
m54 at 0/1 anchors the weak-condition end of an ordinary ketone family and protects the central distribution against corrections learned from late-tail rows such as 5fc00b4a6787d6ea4547.
m29 at 10/1 supplies an ordinary ketone point at a moderate strong ratio, testing whether its response remains central or begins a late completion tail.
m9 at 10/1 fills a middle point in a donor-free aromatic condition curve and can distinguish smooth solvent response from isolated strong-ratio behavior.
m169 at 0/1 adds a low-strength donor-free ketone control with a different flexible side chain, testing transfer of ordinary carbonyl calibration across structural context.
m182 at 0/1 provides a weak-condition fused-carbonyl control before stronger-ratio conditions, helping separate aromatic topology from solvent-strength effects.
m43 at 10/1 is a halogenated ketone condition anchor that extends the observed m43 series toward stronger solvent and tests whether halogenation changes the late-tail gate.
m50 at 50/1 is a strong-ratio neutral halogenated control, directly testing whether a very high PE fraction creates a tail without donor or acceptor functionality.
m184 at 0/1 and high nominal loading supplies a weak-condition loading anchor for a neutral halogenated aldehyde family, separating loading effects from strong PE effects.
m109 at 1/1 provides central calibration for a halogenated anisole-like scaffold at a substantial loading volume, useful for constraining aromatic and halogen effects.
m84 at 10/1 and PE loading extends a donor-free ester response curve into a stronger-ratio regime and tests whether ordinary esters share a common curvature.
m79 at 20/1 samples a high-ratio ester-like condition where completion tails may emerge, supplying a structural comparison to multifunctional and donor-containing failures.
m72 at 2/1 gives a second local point near the onset of the m72 response, allowing the retrained model to learn curvature rather than interpolate only between distant ratios.
m89 at 2/1 probes the lower-strength side of a donor/ester-rich response family and helps connect ordinary retention to the late regimes observed for related ester rows.
m34 at 10/1 tests an ordinary donor-free ketone under PE loading, providing a gate experiment before extrapolating from extreme strong-ratio observations.
m69 at 0/1 is a weak-condition common ketone control that constrains baseline onset and completion behavior before stronger-ratio corrections are applied.
m167 at 10/1 probes a two-carbonyl scaffold whose endpoint can differ from simple ketones, targeting V2 representation and multifunctional-carbonyl calibration.
m41 at 20/1 and low loading volume extends a strong-ratio ketone curve and tests whether a conventional aromatic ketone enters a late regime without donor functionality.
m187 at 5/1 provides an intermediate condition for a halogenated aldehyde, testing whether its observed central behavior remains stable before stronger-ratio extrapolation.
m2 at 10/1 is a donor-free brominated diaryl point that tests solvent response in a rigid aromatic scaffold and supplies a comparison to both weak and very strong ratios.
m81 at 10/1 and larger loading volume samples an ester-rich response region where onset and completion may move differently, improving endpoint-sensitive representation.
m12 at 50/1 extends a hydrophobic donor-free condition curve into the strong-PE regime and serves as a neutral control for deciding when a late-tail correction is justified.
m184 at 10/1 and lower loading volume forms a loading and condition contrast with the weak-condition m184 point, testing whether endpoint shifts are amount-sensitive.
m213 at 20/1 is a strong-ratio diaryl ether control that tests whether weakly interacting aromatic chemistry stays central when PE is high.
m7 at 50/1 provides another neutral high-PE control, helping distinguish generic aromatic solvent response from the scaffold-specific late tails in carbonyl-rich rows.
m143 at 0/1 anchors a donor-free halogenated aldehyde under weak conditions and supports transfer learning across related aromatic aldehyde structures.
m92 at 20/1 with EA loading extends the same-molecule EA curve between measured moderate and very strong conditions, directly testing nonlinear solvent response.
m38 at 2/1 and high loading volume tests loading sensitivity in a rigid aromatic carbonyl scaffold, complementing observed m38 rows across loading and ratio.
m34 at 5/1 and larger volume supplies a matched condition-response point with the selected 10/1 m34 experiment, making the ordinary ketone curve more learnable.
m197 at 2/1 and high loading volume extends an aldehyde curve into a moderate solvent regime and tests whether its V2 behavior is controlled by loading as well as ratio.

hypotheses.content: Solvent-strength response is nonlinear and scaffold-specific: ordinary carbonyls may remain central while multifunctional, donor-containing, and selected ester families cross into late V2 regimes at particular ratios or loading solvents.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local condition curves teach QGeoGNN where a shared solvent-strength trend fails and reduce interpolation errors across central and late-tail rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do ordinary ketones, esters, and multifunctional scaffolds share a ratio threshold, or are their transitions scaffold-specific?

hypotheses.content: V2 completion tails require endpoint-sensitive structural interactions and can be wrong independently of V1, especially for multifunctional, donor-containing, and heteroatom-rich scaffolds.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The retrained model needs endpoint-specific representations instead of transferring onset corrections directly to V2.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which motifs best predict long completion tails after onset: multiple acceptors, HBDs, aromatic carbonyls, or their loading interactions?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading volume interact with strongly retained scaffolds and can shift V1 and V2 differently; the effect is not a simple global loading correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched loading contrasts can prevent the model from attributing amount-driven endpoint shifts to molecule identity or solvent ratio.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do loading contrasts in ester, aldehyde, and multifunctional carbonyl families produce a shared V2 shift or remain molecule-specific?

hypotheses.content: Weakly interacting neutral and halogenated rows are needed to constrain corrections learned from rare high-retention failures, although some neutral scaffolds can still develop strong-ratio tails.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controls prevent a tail-focused retraining round from damaging the common Row-distribution while testing whether neutral chemistry can still show late endpoints.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which neutral controls remain calibrated across strong PE ratios and which require a separate aromatic-size or halogen interaction term?

feedback_interpretation: Recent outcomes support local repair rather than a universal strong-PE correction. The measured m101 contrast 9b612b8b4815d21f4fc6 still had a substantial V2 miss, while m4 971b4f8e32cbdf087dd and m62 b3b38f7212d8649d9ac1 exposed separate endpoint and onset failures. Donor-containing m186 43758e84c67aabf44a9f and phenolic ester m105 a8a8b4ab0ef68c063c29 weakened transfer of the severe polar-tail correction because their V1 and V2 behavior differed. Ordinary ketone m68 cb534927304d5c892100 and neutral controls such as m111 d17718dc009389d217a2 remained much closer. The corrected batch therefore emphasizes local condition and loading curves for tail-prone families while retaining ordinary ketone, halogenated, and diaryl controls.
batch_rationale: The 32 experiments combine condition-response curves, loading contrasts, endpoint repair, and central calibration. m72, m55, m9, m34, m79, m12, m92, m41, m2, and m213 extend solvent curves. m184, m38, m81, m167, and m197 probe loading or endpoint interactions. m54, m69, m50, m109, m143, m187, m7, m3, and m213 provide donor-free and halogenated controls. This balance should improve generalization by separating scaffold-specific V2 tails from broad PE/EA effects and loading effects while protecting accuracy on the common central Row-distribution.
